name: Sentinel
description: Sentinel watches Jellyfin playback sessions and explains, with evidence, why a specific transcode or playback problem happened — not just that it happened.
overview: Evidence-based root-cause diagnosis for Jellyfin playback problems

versions.changelog: Adds plugin-update and restart-pending notifications — a new, user-requested feature not in the original master plan. Sentinel now checks hourly for available plugin updates (any installed plugin, not just itself) and notifies once per distinct plugin+version, deduplicated via a new NotifiedPluginUpdate table so the same update is never re-announced. Separately watches for a pending server restart and notifies exactly once on the transition into that state (never re-fires while already pending). These are deliberately two distinct notifications — an available update does not by itself imply a pending restart — verified against real Jellyfin v12.1 source (IInstallationManager.GetAvailablePluginUpdates, IApplicationHost.HasPendingRestartChanged) rather than assumed. Also: a holistic security review across the full plugin source found zero Critical/High/Medium/Low findings — SQL injection, credential handling, dashboard XSS, and controller authorization were all confirmed clean; one Informational note (outbound webhook/SMTP destinations have no private-IP-range validation) was reviewed and judged a deliberately accepted non-issue given this plugin's real threat model. This release marks completion of the originally-requested MVP scope (localization, Incident Engine, Notification Delivery, modern dashboard) plus every explicitly-requested addition (Series-Episode display, per-incident user tracking, admin sidebar entry, and this plugin-update/restart feature).

Real dashboard visual overhaul, in direct response to live-server feedback that the previous release's UI "still doesn't look good". The Notification Channels settings section (added in 0.1.5.2) was completely unstyled — a long list of plain stacked form fields sitting above the actual incident dashboard, so it was the first thing visible on page load instead of Sentinel's real content. Now: the settings collapse into a closed-by-default accordion so incidents are the first thing visible; each of the four channels (Webhook/Discord/Telegram/Email) gets its own card in a responsive grid with brand-accurate accent colors; test-send results are color-coded (green success / red failure) instead of plain text. Every existing field id and API interaction is unchanged — pure structural/CSS restructuring, reviewed with explicit focus on confirming none of the 18 settings-field ids or 4 channel-name strings drifted during the rewrite. Still not verified in a real browser by this session (no reachable instance here) — this release exists specifically so the user can judge the actual result themselves on their own server.

Adds Notification Delivery — Webhook, Discord, Telegram, and Email (via MailKit) channels, a severity mapping (diagnosis confidence to low/medium/high), and a dedup-aware dispatcher that notifies exactly once per new-or-reopened Incident (never per raw diagnosis or per plain occurrence-count increment). Dashboard gains a per-channel config section (enable, destination/credential fields, minimum-severity threshold, and a mandatory "Send test" button per channel). Also adds: tracking and display of which Jellyfin user hit each diagnosis/incident (never part of the Incident dedup fingerprint, to avoid fragmenting incidents on shared household devices/profiles); Sentinel's own entry in the server admin sidebar under Plugins; an incident filter/count tab bar (All/Active/Acknowledged/Resolved) and a small visual polish pass on the dashboard. One security-relevant fix applied before release: the Email channel initially used SecureSocketOptions.Auto, which can silently fall back to an unencrypted SMTP connection if the server doesn't advertise STARTTLS — changed to StartTls/SslOnConnect, which fail the connection outright instead of downgrading, so SMTP credentials can never be sent in cleartext. Notification Delivery is NOT yet wired to the plugin-update/restart-pending feature (still planned, not in this release) and has not been verified against real Discord/Telegram/Email/webhook endpoints — that needs the admin's own credentials and is tracked as a post-release verification step. Verified by a fresh-subagent review after every task (spec compliance + code quality, including independent re-runs of the full test suite, independent re-derivation of MailKit's exact publish-output dependency list, and independent verification of the TLS-downgrade fix); one real, non-blocking test-coverage gap (the dispatcher's channel-wiring logic) found by a task reviewer was fixed before this release, not left open.

Adds full localization (English, German, Spanish, French, Swedish, Danish, Polish) — a per-plugin Language setting, and every diagnosis explanation/recommendation plus every dashboard UI string is now translated at serve time via a new GET Sentinel/ui-strings endpoint. Fixes the dashboard's media display to show "Series - Episode Name" for TV episodes instead of just the episode name. Adds the Incident Engine: diagnoses sharing the same rule code, media item, client, and device are now deduplicated into a single Incident (via a partial unique SQLite index on that fingerprint) instead of alerting once per raw diagnosis; a resolved incident that recurs reopens instead of duplicating; new GET/POST Sentinel/incidents endpoints (list, acknowledge, resolve). The dashboard is rewritten from a plain diagnosis table into a card-based Incident view with status badges, occurrence counts, and working Acknowledge/Resolve buttons, plus a language selector wired to the new setting. Notification Delivery (Webhook/Discord/Telegram/Email), the plugin-update/restart-pending notification feature, and a dedicated security review are NOT yet in this release — tracked for a following one. Verified by a fresh-subagent review after every task (spec compliance + code quality, including independent re-runs of the full test suite and independent JSON-validity checks on all 7 locale files); not yet confirmed against a real Jellyfin server for any of this release's features.

Adds five new diagnosis rules covering external audio tracks, HDR/dynamic-range mismatches, audio channel downmixing, bitrate-only transcodes, and resolution-only transcodes — including the exact real-world case confirmed on a live server in 0.1.4.0 (an AV1 transcode with only an audio-channel-downmix reason, previously unrecognized). Also wires up the previously dormant Known Core Issues table into the API and dashboard, surfaced as a distinct "Known Jellyfin Bug" note. Verified by three rounds of independent review; each rule's PlayMethod == Transcode gate and mutual exclusivity with stronger, more specific diagnoses is covered by a dedicated regression test, verified RED/GREEN by temporarily removing every gate and confirming each one is independently caught. Not yet confirmed against a real server for these specific new rules.

Fixes a data-integrity bug confirmed on a real server running 0.1.3.0: a session with a verified, active ffmpeg transcode (video re-encoded, audio downmixed — confirmed via the server's own transcode log) still produced a PlaybackEvent row with PlayMethod = DirectPlay next to a correctly non-zero TranscodeReasons, silently suppressing the diagnosis despite the reasons having been captured correctly. PlaybackEventFactory now forces PlayMethod to Transcode when TranscodeReasons is non-default and PlayMethod resolved to DirectPlay or null (DirectStream/remux sessions are correctly left alone, since they legitimately carry non-zero TranscodeReasons too — a broader first version of this fix was caught and narrowed during review before release). Verified by two rounds of independent review plus a regression test reproducing the exact real-world contradiction; not yet re-confirmed against a real server for this specific fix.

Fixes a bug affecting every previous version: Jellyfin always clears the play method and transcode-reason data on a session before firing the event this plugin used to read them from, so PlaybackEvent rows were recorded with an empty play method and zero transcode reasons regardless of whether a transcode actually happened — confirmed live with a real bitrate-driven transcode that produced a blank database row despite Jellyfin's own dashboard showing an active transcode with a specific reason. Sentinel now also listens to playback-progress events (while that data is still live) and caches it per playback, including a fallback for Jellyfin's own idle-timeout stop path, which never supplies the identifier this plugin would otherwise key on. Verified by three rounds of independent review plus targeted regression tests reproducing the exact real-world event sequence; not yet re-confirmed against a real server for this specific fix.

Adds a minimal read-only dashboard to the plugin's configuration page: recent diagnoses (media, client/device, confidence, explanation) with click-to-expand evidence, backed by a new admin-only API endpoint. Verified by code inspection, two independent review rounds, and a clean local build/test run; not yet independently confirmed against a real server for this specific feature.

Fixes a confirmed bug in 0.1.0.0: installing on a real Jellyfin server resulted in status 'Malfunctioned' because of native SQLite library loading (see build.yaml changelog for the full root cause). Confirmed loading and running correctly on a real Jellyfin 12.1 server. 0.1.0.0 is removed from this list since it is confirmed broken.
